summary.p: This page documents the relevant standards that the Apache HTTP Server implements or follows, along with brief descriptions.
In addition to the information listed below, the following resources should be consulted:

ul.li: RFC Errata - Errata for published RFCs
HTTP Working Group Specifications - A pre-compiled list of HTTP related RFCs and drafts

section.title: HTTP
section.p: Regardless of what modules are compiled and used, Apache as a basic web server complies with the following IETF standards:

dl.dd: Defines the semantics shared by all versions of HTTP: methods, status codes, header and trailer fields, content negotiation, and message metadata. Obsoletes RFC 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, and 7694.
Defines HTTP caches and the associated header fields that control cache behavior or indicate cacheable response messages. Obsoletes RFC 7234.
Defines the HTTP/1.1 message syntax and connection management. Obsoletes RFC 7230.
Defines an optimized expression of HTTP semantics using binary framing and multiplexed streams over a single TCP connection. Obsoletes RFC 7540 and 8740.
Defines the mapping of HTTP semantics over QUIC, providing similar features to HTTP/2 with reduced latency.
The original HTTP/1.0 specification. Retained for historical reference; httpd still accepts HTTP/1.0 requests.

dl.dt: 3986 (Standards Track) - Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax
dl.dd: The generic syntax and resolution rules for Uniform Resource Identifiers. Obsoletes RFC 2396.
Defines a compact sequence of characters for describing a range of URIs through variable expansion.

section.title: TLS/SSL
section.p: The following standards apply when mod_ssl is enabled:

dl.dd: The current version of the Transport Layer Security protocol, providing communications privacy over the Internet. Obsoletes RFC 5246 (TLS 1.2 specification text).
The previous widely-deployed version of TLS. Still supported by httpd for compatibility with older clients.
The Online Certificate Status Protocol, used for checking certificate revocation status in real time (OCSP stapling via SSLStaplingCache).
Defines TLS extensions including Server Name Indication (SNI), which httpd uses for name-based virtual hosting over TLS.

section.title: Authentication
section.p: Concerning the different methods of authentication:

dl.dd: HTTP Basic authentication, transmitting credentials as user-id/password pairs encoded in Base64. Obsoletes RFC 2617 (Basic auth portion).
HTTP Digest authentication, providing a challenge-response mechanism that avoids sending the password in cleartext. Obsoletes RFC 2617 (Digest auth portion).
Proactive and reactive content negotiation, including the Accept, Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding, and Accept-Charset header fields.
Defines the Brotli compression algorithm, supported via mod_brotli.
Defines the Forwarded header field for conveying information about the client-facing side of proxy servers.
dl.dt: 9209 (Standards Track) - The Proxy-Status HTTP Response Header Field
dl.dd: Defines a mechanism for proxies to communicate the details of intermediary handling to the client.
Defines a mechanism for running the WebSocket protocol over a single HTTP/2 stream.
Defines the WebSocket protocol, enabling two-way communication between a client and server over a single TCP connection. Supported via mod_proxy_wstunnel.
Defines the Common Gateway Interface for running external programs on a web server. Implemented by mod_cgi and mod_cgid.

dl.dt: 4918 (Standards Track) - HTTP Extensions for Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV)
dl.dd: Defines extensions to HTTP for distributed authoring operations. Obsoletes RFC 2518.
dl.dt: 3744 (Standards Track) - Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV) Access Control Protocol
dl.dd: Defines access control extensions to WebDAV.

section.title: Language/Country Codes
section.p: Language and country codes used in content negotiation:

dl.dd: ISO 639 provides two sets of language codes, one as a two-letter code set (639-1) and another as a three-letter code set (this part of ISO 639) for the representation of names of languages.
Country names and corresponding alpha-2 and alpha-3 code elements.
dl.dt: 5646 (Best Current Practice) - Tags for Identifying Languages
dl.dd: Describes the structure and registry of language tags used in HTTP content negotiation (Accept-Language, Content-Language). Obsoletes RFC 3066.
Defines the Content-Language and Accept-Language header fields for indicating language preferences in HTTP messages.
